name: Chandragiri Hills
tagline: A 10-minute cable car to 2,551 m and a Himalayan skyline
meta_description: Chandragiri Hills guide: cable car from Thankot to 2,551 m, fares for Indians and foreigners, Bhaleshwor Mahadev temple, forest hike and best time to go.
summary: Chandragiri Hills is a 2,551 m ridge on the south-west rim of the Kathmandu Valley, reached by a 2.4 km cable car from Thankot in about 10 minutes. On clear mornings it shows a long Himalayan skyline and the whole valley below. At the top are the Bhaleshwor Mahadev temple, viewing decks and a resort.
intro: Chandragiri gives the most height for the least effort anywhere around Kathmandu. A gondola lifts you about 1,000 m from the base station at Thankot to the 2,551 m summit ridge in 9 to 12 minutes, over oak and rhododendron forest that drops away steeply beneath the cabin. At the top, the valley floor lies spread out to the north-east, with Kathmandu's sprawl, the Swayambhunath hill and the airport runway all easy to pick out. Behind them, on a good morning, snow peaks run along the horizon for more than 200 km.

The ridge has history as well as views. Before the Tribhuvan Rajpath road opened in 1956, the main route into the valley from India climbed from Bhimphedi through Chitlang and crossed the Chandragiri pass, so generations of traders, envoys and porters walked over this hill. Nepali tradition also says Prithvi Narayan Shah looked down on the valley from Chandragiri and resolved to conquer it. Today the summit belongs to the Shiva temple of Bhaleshwor Mahadev, pilgrims, families on day trips and the hilltop resort.

Timing makes or breaks a Chandragiri visit. From October to February, the first cars of the morning give the best chance of a clear Himalayan panorama; by noon, cloud and haze often close in. In the monsoon, June to September, you may see nothing but mist. The top is usually 6 to 8 °C cooler than Kathmandu and windy, so bring a jacket in every season. We schedule it early, often paired with Kirtipur or Swayambhunath in the afternoon.

highlights.title: Cable car over the forest to 2,551 m
highlights.text: The 2.4 km gondola line opened in 2016 and runs eight-seat cabins from Thankot to the summit in 9 to 12 minutes. It climbs steadily over thick forest with the valley opening behind you. Ask to sit facing downhill on the way up for the best view of Kathmandu.

highlights.title: A Himalayan skyline from Annapurna eastward
highlights.text: On clear mornings, mostly October to February, the summit deck looks along a line of peaks that the operators list from Annapurna and Manaslu in the west, through Ganesh Himal and Langtang, to Gauri Shankar in the east. Peak identification boards help. Cloud usually builds by late morning.

highlights.title: Bhaleshwor Mahadev temple at the summit
highlights.text: A short walk from the top station brings you to Bhaleshwor Mahadev, a Shiva shrine whose name tradition links to the forehead, bhala, of the goddess Sati. Pilgrims come especially on Mondays, during the month of Shrawan and at Maha Shivaratri. The temple area is open to visitors of all faiths.

highlights.title: The whole Kathmandu Valley at your feet
highlights.text: From the north side of the ridge the valley looks like a relief map: the Bagmati threading through the city, Swayambhunath on its hill, the airport runway and the far rim at Nagarkot. Late afternoons in winter can be clear enough for city photography, and the lights come on as the last cars descend.

highlights.title: Forest trails on foot
highlights.text: Fit walkers can skip the gondola on the way up and climb through the Chandragiri forest from Thankot in three to four hours, gaining about 1,000 m. Trails also run along the ridge and down the south side towards Chitlang. Most hikers ride the cable car down to save their knees.

highlights.title: A family day out near the city
highlights.text: The summit has viewing decks, cafes, a restaurant, children's play areas and short paved paths, which makes Chandragiri one of the easiest outings for grandparents and young children. Cabins take wheelchairs with assistance, and children shorter than about 3 feet ride free; check current status before you travel.

how_to_reach.text: The base station is at Thankot, ≈ 14 km west of Thamel on the Tribhuvan Highway via Kalanki. Allow 45 minutes early in the morning and up to 1.5 hours in daytime traffic. Private cars park at the station; local buses for Thankot leave from Kalanki for about NPR 30–50. A taxi from Thamel costs roughly NPR 1,200–1,800 one way.

A forest trail climbs from the Thankot side to the summit, roughly 3–4 hours and about 1,000 m of ascent on steep, sometimes loose paths. A longer route links Chandragiri with the Champadevi ridge and Chitlang village to the south. Go with a guide, start early and carry water, as there are few shops on the way.

Tribhuvan International Airport is ≈ 20 km away on the opposite side of the city, so allow 1 to 1.5 hours by car to Thankot depending on traffic. We sometimes fit Chandragiri in on arrival day for guests landing early, since the drive skirts the old city via the Ring Road.

where_to_stay: Most guests visit Chandragiri as a half-day trip from Kathmandu, staying in Thamel, Lazimpat or Naxal and leaving at 7 to 7.30 am to catch the clearest light. For a night on the hill, Chandragiri Hills Resort sits on the summit ridge and is reached only by the cable car; it reopened with the gondola in November 2025 after the September protests. Staying overnight means sunset and the next morning's sunrise on the ridge without the day crowds, and the resort has included cable car rides for its guests; check current status before you travel. Kirtipur and the western edge of Kathmandu around Kalanki are closer bases, but have few hotels of note.
tips: Take one of the first cable cars of the day, as clouds usually cover the peaks by 11 am even in clear-weather months.
Avoid Saturdays and public holidays if you can; queues at the Thankot base station can stretch past an hour at peak times.
Carry a warm layer and a windproof jacket, since the summit is typically 6 to 8 °C colder than Kathmandu and can touch freezing on winter mornings.
Indian passport or voter ID holders should carry ID to the ticket counter to qualify for the SAARC fare.
Cable cars pause in strong wind, thunderstorms and power cuts, so keep your afternoon plans flexible on a Chandragiri day.

experiences.title: Chandragiri cable car ride and summit decks
experiences.best_time: First cars of the morning, Oct–Feb
experiences.summary: A 2.4 km gondola ride from Thankot to the 2,551 m Chandragiri ridge in about 10 minutes, followed by time on the summit decks for Himalayan and valley views. Easy, quick and suited to every age, as long as you go early enough to beat the clouds.
body: Our driver collects you around 7 am so you reach the Thankot base station as it opens. Opened in 2016, the line uses 38 eight-seat gondolas built with Austrian technology and carries about 1,000 people an hour, so queues move fast on weekdays. The ride takes 9 to 12 minutes and climbs about 1,000 m, crossing ridges of forest where you can sometimes spot langur monkeys and eagles riding the morning air. The lower station was set on fire during the September 2025 protests; the system was repaired, safety-tested and reopened in November 2025.

At the top, walk a few minutes to the main viewing deck and the peak identification boards. On a clear day the skyline runs from the Annapurna and Manaslu massifs in the west through Ganesh Himal and Langtang to Gauri Shankar. The Kathmandu Valley spreads out to the north-east, and the temple of Bhaleshwor Mahadev stands on the highest point. Give yourself 1.5 to 2 hours on top for the views, the temple, a hot drink and a slow wander along the paved paths.

Return fares at our last check were about US$ 22 to 23 for foreigners, about NPR 1,280 to 1,320 for SAARC nationals including Indians, and about NPR 800 for Nepalis, with discounts for seniors, students and children; check current status before you travel. Operations stop in high winds, thunderstorms and occasionally for maintenance. Guests with a strong fear of heights usually manage well, since the cabins are enclosed and the ride is smooth, but a downhill-facing seat can feel more exposed.

faqs.q: What is the Chandragiri cable car ticket price for Indians?
faqs.a: Indian nationals pay the SAARC fare, which was about NPR 1,280 to 1,320 for a return ride at our last check, roughly ₹800 to ₹830. Foreigners pay about US$ 22 to 23 return, and Nepalis about NPR 800. Fares are revised often and discounts apply for seniors, students and small children, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long is the Chandragiri cable car ride?
faqs.a: The ride covers 2.4 km and takes about 9 to 12 minutes each way, climbing roughly 1,000 m from Thankot to the 2,551 m summit. Including the drive from Kathmandu, queues and time at the top, plan on four to five hours for the whole outing, or a little more on weekends.

faqs.q: Is the Chandragiri cable car open after the 2025 protests?
faqs.a: Yes. The lower station was badly damaged by fire on 9 September 2025, and services were suspended while the system was repaired and inspected. The cable car and the hilltop resort reopened on 8 November 2025. Short closures for maintenance or weather still occur, so check current status before you travel.

experiences.title: Bhaleshwor Mahadev darshan on Chandragiri
experiences.best_time: Monday mornings, Shrawan (Jul–Aug) and Maha Shivaratri
experiences.price_hint: Free entry; cable car fare applies
experiences.summary: Darshan and puja at Bhaleshwor Mahadev, the Shiva temple on the 2,551 m summit of Chandragiri, linked by tradition to the place where Sati's forehead fell. A short, easy pilgrimage that Indian families often add to Pashupatinath on a Kathmandu temple tour.
body: Bhaleshwor Mahadev takes its name from bhala, the forehead. Hindu tradition, recorded in the Himavatkhanda, tells how Shiva carried the body of his wife Sati across the world after her death at Daksha's sacrifice, and how her body fell in pieces at sacred sites. The forehead is said to have fallen here on Chandragiri. For pilgrims from India who have already prayed at Pashupatinath and Guhyeshwari in Kathmandu, the temple completes a Shiva and Shakti circuit around the valley.

The shrine stands a few minutes' walk from the top station, on the highest point of the ridge, with prayer bells and a stone platform facing the mountains. Priests are present through the day to help with simple puja, and flowers, incense and offerings can be bought at the summit. Mondays, sacred to Shiva, are busier, as is the monsoon month of Shrawan in July and August, when many devotees climb on foot. Maha Shivaratri in February or March brings large crowds and long cable car queues.

Entry to the temple is free, though the cable car fare applies; donations are welcome. Shoes come off before the inner area, and leather items are best left behind. Non-Hindu visitors are welcome to watch respectfully. We usually time darshan for the first hour after the cable car opens, so you pray in quiet and still catch the clearest mountain view. Festival-day timings and crowd arrangements change from year to year, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the story of Bhaleshwor Mahadev?
faqs.a: Bhaleshwor means lord of the forehead. Tradition holds that when Shiva carried Sati's body after her death at Daksha's yagna, her forehead, or bhala, fell on Chandragiri, and Shiva manifested here as Bhaleshwor. The temple on the summit ridge marks that spot and is an important Shiva shrine for Nepali and Indian pilgrims.

faqs.q: Can non-Hindus visit Bhaleshwor Mahadev temple?
faqs.a: Yes. Visitors of all faiths can walk around the temple and watch worship respectfully. Remove shoes where asked, avoid photographing people at prayer without permission, and do not touch offerings. On crowded festival days, priests may ask non-worshippers to stand back from the inner area so devotees can complete their puja.

faqs.q: Is Chandragiri crowded on Maha Shivaratri?
faqs.a: Yes. Maha Shivaratri, in February or March, is one of the busiest days of the year at Chandragiri, with long queues at the cable car and around the temple. If you want to be there on the day, arrive at opening time. Most of our Shivaratri guests focus on Pashupatinath and visit Chandragiri on a quieter day.

experiences.title: Hike up Chandragiri through the forest
experiences.price_hint: ≈ ₹3,500 per person with guide, car and one-way cable car
experiences.summary: A steep half-day hike from the Thankot side to the 2,551 m summit, climbing about 1,000 m through oak and rhododendron forest, then riding the cable car down. Good preparation for a trek and a far quieter way to reach the top than the gondola queue.
body: We start from the Thankot side early, ideally by 7 am, to walk in the cool of the morning. The trail climbs straight into forest and keeps climbing: about 1,000 m of height gain in 3 to 4 hours, on dirt paths, stone steps and a few loose, eroded sections. Oak, chestnut and rhododendron shade most of the route, and the rhododendrons bloom red from March to April. There are few signboards and several junctions, which is why we send a local guide.

Regular rest stops open views back over the valley floor, and you may hear barking deer or see langur monkeys in the canopy. The final stretch joins the ridge near the summit, where the temple of Bhaleshwor Mahadev and the top station appear quite suddenly after hours of trees. Fit hikers who trek regularly find it a solid workout; anyone who walks only occasionally should expect sore calves the next day. The 2,551 m summit is too low for altitude sickness to be a concern.

At the top, rest with tea and the view before taking the cable car down in about 10 minutes; one-way tickets are sold at the top station, priced at a little over half the return fare; check current status before you travel. Carry 2 litres of water, snacks, a light jacket and sturdy shoes with grip. Avoid the trail in the monsoon, June to September, when it turns slippery and leeches are common. In dry season, keep an eye out for wildfire smoke in March and April.

faqs.q: How hard is the Chandragiri hike?
faqs.a: It is a steep, moderate hike: about 1,000 m of climbing in 3 to 4 hours on forest paths with loose sections and stone steps. Anyone who walks regularly can manage it at a steady pace. It is a good fitness test before a trek, and riding the cable car down removes the hardest part for knees.

faqs.q: Can I hike up Chandragiri and take the cable car down?
faqs.a: Yes, that is the way most hikers do it. One-way cable car tickets are sold at the summit station, costing a little over half the return fare, and the ride down takes about 10 minutes. Our driver waits at the Thankot base station to take you back to Kathmandu.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for the Chandragiri forest trail?
faqs.a: We strongly recommend one. The trail has several unsigned junctions, few people on weekdays and patchy phone signal in places, and walkers do get lost. A local guide keeps you on the right path, sets a sensible pace and knows where water and rest stops are. Solo hikers should at least share their plan with someone.

Yes, if you go on a clear morning. For a 10-minute cable car ride you reach 2,551 m and, between October and February, see a Himalayan skyline plus the whole Kathmandu Valley. On cloudy days the views shrink to forest and mist, so we keep it flexible in our itineraries and move it to the clearest morning of your stay.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Chandragiri Hills?
faqs.a: October to February is best, and early morning is essential: the first cable cars give the clearest mountain views before cloud builds around late morning. March and April are warmer with more haze but bring rhododendron blooms. From June to September monsoon cloud often hides everything, though the temple and cable car keep running.

faqs.q: How do I get to the Chandragiri cable car from Thamel?
faqs.a: The base station is at Thankot, about 14 km west of Thamel via Kalanki and the Tribhuvan Highway. A private car or taxi takes 45 minutes early in the morning and up to 1.5 hours in daytime traffic; a taxi costs roughly NPR 1,200 to 1,800 one way. Local buses also run to Thankot from Kalanki.

faqs.q: Can I see Mount Everest from Chandragiri?
faqs.a: Do not count on it. The skyline from Chandragiri runs from Annapurna and Manaslu in the west to Langtang and Gauri Shankar in the east, and the operators say Everest can appear on exceptionally clear days. For a reliable view of Everest itself, the Everest mountain flight from Kathmandu is the better choice.

faqs.q: How cold is it at the top of Chandragiri?
faqs.a: The summit is usually 6 to 8 °C cooler than Kathmandu. Winter mornings can be around 0 to 5 °C with frost, and brief light snow has fallen in cold January and February spells. Even in spring and autumn, the wind on the ridge makes a fleece and windproof jacket worthwhile.

faqs.q: What are the Chandragiri cable car timings?
faqs.a: The cable car runs during daytime hours, opening at around 9 am on most days and running into the late afternoon, with longer hours on some weekends and holidays. Operations pause in strong wind, thunderstorms and for maintenance. Timings change by season, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Chandragiri suitable for elderly visitors and small children?
faqs.a: Yes. The cable car does all the climbing, and the summit has paved paths, benches, cafes and toilets, so grandparents and small children manage easily. Staff help with wheelchairs boarding the cabins. The temple platform involves a few steps, and the cold wind can tire young children, so bring warm layers.

faqs.q: Can I stay overnight on Chandragiri?
faqs.a: Yes. Chandragiri Hills Resort sits on the summit ridge and is reached by the cable car, which lets you see sunset and sunrise without the daytime crowds. It reopened with the cable car in November 2025. Most visitors still come for a half day and sleep in Kathmandu, about 14 km away.

faqs.q: How long do I need for a Chandragiri trip?
faqs.a: Plan four to five hours from Kathmandu: up to 1.5 hours driving each way, 10 minutes on the cable car each way, and 1.5 to 2 hours on top. Hikers going up on foot should allow six to seven hours in total. Adding Kirtipur or Swayambhunath afterwards makes a full, easy day.
